title: With having ai comes responsibility
author: Affectionate_Fact854
selftext:
I see everywhere so many people now just churning out SaaS,apps, cross reverse games and more.

That in itself is great and I love it ,but what I'm also picking up more then ever is the following.

Incompetent people that has the mindset of ai can do the development "so I don't need to bother learning to code."

The implications I'm seeing of that is , seeing games that would have been made in the 1990's that was able to run almost on a toaster,  that now either requires to run on 8gig ram , or requires a serious graphics card...

Your apps or games is working, but that hardware requirements for the most simplistic and low graphics games shows 1 serious problem.

That problem is scaling,  trusting ai fully,without being able to instruct it on archetecture, and not being able to understand the code means you just don't know when to fork the development into a direction before it becomes a mess..

  
"This is with basic games, now think ,how would you be able to scale a serious game with no technical , coding or art software knowledge..."

  
Ai should not excuse you from doing the effort of learning coding foundations...

NOW is the best time ever to actually starting your journey to learn how to read code, it's easer then it has ever been made in history to pick up a language and learn it.

You don't need to deal with stack overflow,

You don't need to pay for courses,

You dont need to follow YouTube videos, 

Ai can literally punch out learning materials with examples, with tests , for almost free....

  
I encourage you to not be ignorant if your serious about wanting to become a developer please....

comments.author: Count_JohnnyJ
comments.body: Couldn't you just tell it to learn proper architecture and scaling by doing in depth research online? I've had mine go online to learn many things.

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Sure you can.
Still doesn't mean the ai won't hallucinate.
Doesn't mean ai will give you the best solutions without knowing how to phrase your prompts, or when to stop it from burning tokens on something pointless either 

Also you gain no new skills with simply refusing to learn.

Good luck with interviews if you ever want a coding carreer without learning the fundamentals.

Like I said your generation is the luckiest ever having it the easiest ever in history to upskill 

To refuse it is just wild.

replies.author: bunnyUFO
replies.body:
u/Count_JohnnyJ  & u/Affectionate_Fact854   
I think if used in the right way you can learn as you use it to build something too. You don't want to offload thinking entirely, but can let it do/decide things for you too. The power of AI is to make development cycle faster so you actually get to think and decide more things quickly!  
  
A prompt like:  
"I want to build x feature" VS  
"I want to build x feature,  
I believe x architecture would be good because ....   
Does that sound good or can you suggest a different approach?  
Please compare pros and cons"

The first one offloads thinking.  
The second one makes you think and learn more than if you actually coded hand.  
You still get to design software and learn, but make the lull in between smaller.  
You'll likely learn and and have more experience with design patterns doing this than regular development by hand.

If you don't understand something why not watch a video or read blog about it?  
You can even ask the AI agent to give you references to learn and understand the approach better.

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body: If only this was the mindset of vibe coders today....

replies.author: bunnyUFO
replies.body:
I mean it doesn't necessarily have to be code they learn about using AI.  
My same advice could also be for 2D art, 3D art, movie/video production, game design, user experience (UX), animation principles, computer graphics (shaders, render pipeline), character design, story writing, anything really.

If you have a genuine interest in something use it to learn while making the less interesting parts easier to get through.

You should use AI to agument your strengths and cover for weaknesees.  
  
If you genuinely don't want to learn to code and are making a game that is simple from software perspective, that's okay! If you don't want to learn 3D modeling and animation, but want to get move involved in software development that good too!

Just please don't offload all thinking away! Take a genuine interest in improving your own critical thinking and other skills while augmented by AI.

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Your a man of good perspective! 

I mean for me aswell, prior ai I was coding manually , using ai has improved my own knowledge, helped me develop better archetecture , showed me different optimization strategies,  list can go on.

The reason why is simple , if I develop with ai, I always ask it to first pitch me the plan, I read it, ask questions , change parts of his reasoning until the phase plans looks solid. 

If I read something I don't yet understand or have used,  I open a second prompt to deep dive in the topic before going back. 

It has helped me personally grow as a developer much faster then when I was learning from internet and guides.

I even used ai to set up guides and training materials for me to learn how to use "opentoonz, inkscape and asperites " more effectively then surface level, I hate doing art , but it sure does help knowing my way around quickly making changes manually 

Like you said it can apply to any fields
